correctness.rationale: The global-depolarization partial transpose splits into independent pair blocks with eigenvalues q/d²±(1−q)√(x_ix_j), so NPT survival depends monotonically on m=max√(x_ix_j). For s≥1/2, identity s+2m²=t²+Σremaining x_j²≤t²+(1−t)²≤1 is sharp precisely for two-level input. For s≤1/2, AM–GM on top two and Cauchy on remaining d−2 give s≥2m²+(1−2m)²/(d−2) whenever m≥1/d, and solving the increasing function yields the claimed sharp branch; m<1/d is automatically bounded. Equality cases are explicitly realized and normalized. Checks of 8,016 equality/population cases completed. The proof, not finite tests, covers all real s and all integer d≥3.

originality.rationale: Ali et al. 2606.16695 explicitly derives the pairwise global-noise NPT criterion and equal-population threshold, which is credited. The new claim is the *all diagonal-purity strata* sharp optimization and complete equality cases, including a nonmonotone robustness frontier peaking at s=1/2, not a derivation of the already known pairwise spectrum. Independent local-noise flat-support optimization addresses a different channel and restricted input class, so it does not imply this global-noise all-spectrum problem. value.rationale: Diagonal purity Σ|c_j|⁴ is the experimentally meaningful collision probability/inverse participation ratio of input basis measurements. A device choosing coherent populations under a fixed participation budget needs a sharp NPT survival noise guarantee. This theorem supplies the complete exact frontier, all extremizers, a dimension-independent support-changing threshold s=1/2, and the counterintuitive fact that equal occupation of only two levels outlasts an equal-population d-level input under global depolarization. This is a natural full-parameter optimization rather than an arbitrary numerical slice or a claimed improvement in unrelated channel models.
